newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-MAN sees higher sales, steady profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-MAN sees higher sales, steady profits.

text.p: German truckmaker and engineering company MAN AG said on Thursday that better economic conditions abroad would boost sales and production this year, but that profits would remain steady.

In a report on its first half results, MAN said net profit in the first six months of the 1996/97 business year ending June 30 fell to 80 million marks ($47.4 million) from 110 million marks during the same period the year before.

"From today's viewpoint, continued positive market developments and domestic tax relief are a good starting point to make up for the first half and make a profit matching the year before," MAN said in a statement.

The lower first half profit figure came despite a two percent increase in sales to 8.81 billion marks. The company said that ongoing rationalisation efforts and fierce competition that limits margins would inhibit profit growth during the year.
Sales climbed largely due to stronger sales of diesel motors and machine and plant equipment.

But sales at MAN's major units declined during the period. The company's truckmaking operations reported a five percent decline in sales to 3.63 billion marks and its printing machine unit saw sales fall 12 percent to 889 million marks.
The figures came as something of a disappointment to share traders who had been looking for the company to show a clear financial improvement.
Chairman Kluas Goette had said in December "positive developments at MAN are continuing and another good result should be made." MAN shares fell nine marks to 433.50 in floor trade in Frankfurt.
In the 1995/96 business year ending June 30, MAN made a group net profit of 330 million marks, up from 272 million marks the year before.
MAN said its expected sales and incoming orders to climb during the year, mostly due to better markets in North America and in Asia.
Incoming orders in the first half of this year climbed nine percent to 11 billion marks.
"The favourable developments in incoming orders...supports expectations for higher production and sales in the second half of the business year," the statement said.
MAN's printing machine unit made a separate statement from the parent, saying that will again report a loss for the full business year.
MAN Roland suffered a 81 million mark loss in 1995/96, less than a 145.7 million mark loss the year before.
